rule.description: Production code in the ngx_cache_purge module translation unit that has no reachable execution path under the supported nginx module entry points: internal-linkage functions and module state that no live directive, handler, merge or registration path ever references, and value computations inside live functions whose stored results no live statement consumes.

checks.description: Detect internal-linkage functions defined in the module that no live configuration, request, merge or registration path references.
checks.detected_relation: defined static function -> zero references anywhere in the translation unit, including the module registration tables
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A function with internal linkage that nothing in the module references can never be reached through nginx directive dispatch, content handlers or module callbacks, so it has no role under supported uses.

matches.evidence: clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-function: no reference to this static function exists anywhere in the translation unit; it is not listed in ngx_command_t, ngx_http_module_t or any handler path.
clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-function: the purge-key prefix matcher has no callers; the live purge path never computes or matches key prefixes.
clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-function: the alternative text/plain response renderer is unreachable; the success page is rendered solely by the live send_response path.
clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-function: the matched-entries logging helper has no invocation site in any handler or purge path.
clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-function: the per-entry removal helper duplicates the purge accounting already performed by the live ngx_http_file_cache_purge and is never called.

checks.description: Detect module file-scope state never referenced by any reachable code path.
checks.detected_relation: defined static module-level state -> zero references in the translation unit
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Module-local constants that no reachable code reads are dead state left behind by the retired responsibility.

matches.evidence: clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-const-variable: the response hint string is never read by any code path.
clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-const-variable: the pattern token table is defined but never consumed by any scanning or matching code.

checks.description: Detect computations inside live request and configuration functions whose stored results are never read by any subsequent statement.
checks.detected_relation: value stored to a local -> no later read on any control-flow path through the live function
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Code that executes but computes values that nothing ever consumes is residue of the retired responsibility; removing the computation and its declaration does not change observable behaviour.

matches.evidence: clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-but-set-variable and clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores: the fastcgi purge handler snapshots the shared cache list after locating the zone, and no live statement ever reads it.

clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-but-set-variable and clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores: the access-phase handler scans the incoming method name for a marker character that no live statement consults.
clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-but-set-variable and clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores: the response builder computes the length of a match-summary line that no response path emits.

clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-but-set-variable and clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores: the cache zone count is recorded during zone lookup but never influences the selected zone; the local shares its declaration with the live loop counter, so removing it requires an in-place declaration edit.
clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-but-set-variable and clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores: the purge key length is snapshotted after cache key evaluation and never used afterwards.
clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-but-set-variable and clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores: the purge handler records whether the purge succeeded, but no live statement ever reads the result.

clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-but-set-variable and clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores: the freed size is recorded inside the shared-memory accounting branch but never read by any purge statement.

clang-tidy clang-diagnostic-unused-but-set-variable and clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores: the directive parser scans the configured purge method for an embedded marker character whose result is never consulted.

coverage_notes: E1 is the single file-level location of this module and covers three file-scope members of the retired work: the unreferenced response-hint constant ngx_http_cache_purge_wildcard_hint (ngx_cache_purge_module.c:213), the unreferenced token table ngx_http_cache_purge_wildcard_tokens (ngx_cache_purge_module.c:217), and the write-only ngx_http_cache_purge_loc_conf_t member report_handler (ngx_cache_purge_module.c:67). The first two are detected by the unreferenced-module-state check; the member carries no backend match because the Clang-Tidy diagnostic set backing this rule has no check for struct-member read-reachability.

E15 is the merge-time seed of the report_handler member (ngx_cache_purge_module.c:1929-1930) inside ngx_http_cache_purge_merge_loc_conf, together with its zero-initialisation note in the create_loc_conf comment (ngx_cache_purge_module.c:1810). The location configuration type is private to this translation unit, and the only assignment reads the core location handler slot into the member; no live or dead statement ever dispatches through it, so the member and its seed have no reachable role and carry no backend match. They remain part of the canonical inventory and of the cleanup obligation stated by the task and the downstream rubrics.

Every backend match above was produced by running the exact entrypoint /logs/artifacts/case/smell_check.sh against the injected state: 5 unreferenced functions, 2 unreferenced constants, 8 unconsumed value computations.

The five forward declarations of the unreferenced helpers (ngx_cache_purge_module.c:107-115) belong to E2, E3, E7, E8 and E9 respectively; removing a helper without removing its declaration leaves the rule satisfied only after the declaration is cleared as well, and reverting a declaration alone exposes its definition.

excluded.reason: Compile-time compatibility paths retained on purpose for other supported nginx releases; paths preprocessed out of this build are not reachable code of this binary and are not part of the rule.

excluded.structure: #else /* !NGX_HTTP_CACHE */ module stub at the end of the file
excluded.reason: Alternative build-time implementation for cache-less nginx builds, not unreachable residue.

excluded.structure: externally linked directive, conf, handler and content-handler functions listed in ngx_http_cache_purge_module_commands and ngx_http_cache_purge_module_ctx
excluded.reason: Registered entry points that nginx dispatches from configuration and request processing, therefore reachable by supported production paths.

excluded.structure: shared live helpers (ngx_http_cache_purge_access, ngx_http_cache_purge_conf, ngx_http_fastcgi_cache_purge_handler and the other three protocol purge handlers, ngx_http_cache_purge_cache_get, ngx_http_cache_purge_init, ngx_http_cache_purge_handler, ngx_http_file_cache_purge, ngx_http_cache_purge_send_response)
excluded.reason: Referenced by live configuration and request paths; they host residue sites but are not themselves dead code.
